core_obligations: Reduce to bounding the first direct image (proof lines 2245-2258): for a normal modification of the spectrum of the ring one has to bound the first cohomology of the structure sheaf; by Grauert-Riemenschneider the pushforward of the dualizing module coincides with its zeroth pushforward, so that the trace map becomes a map of modules on the base as in the statement.

Turn the trace map into an Ext group (proof lines 2258-2270): duality expresses the pushforward of the dualizing module as the derived hom of the pushforward of the structure sheaf into the dualizing complex of the base; applying the derived hom to the distinguished triangle relating the structure sheaf to its first direct image yields a short exact sequence whose third term is the second Ext group of the first direct image, the other Ext groups vanishing.

Identify that Ext group as a Matlis dual (proof lines 2270-2282): the first direct image is supported at the closed point, so local duality identifies the second Ext group with the Matlis dual of the first direct image, and since Matlis duality is an equivalence of categories, an element annihilating the Ext group also annihilates the first direct image; consequently the first cohomology of the modification is annihilated by the given element.

Conclude (proof lines 2282-2286): the boundedness required for reduction to rational singularities now follows from the chapter's bound on the torsion of the first cohomology together with the identification of that torsion with the cokernel in question.
proof_roadmap: Use Grauert-Riemenschneider to make the trace map a map of modules on the base and reduce to bounding the first direct image.
Apply duality and the distinguished triangle to exhibit the cokernel of the trace map as a second Ext group of the first direct image.
Identify that Ext group as a Matlis dual, transport the annihilation and finish with the chapter's torsion bound.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a two dimensional local normal Nagata domain with a dualizing complex, the existence of a nonzero element annihilating the cokernel of the trace map for every normal modification implies that reduction to rational singularities is possible (statement lines 2232-2243). The proof (proof lines 2245-2288) uses Grauert-Riemenschneider to treat the trace map as a map of modules, applies duality and a distinguished triangle to express its cokernel as a second Ext group, identifies that group as a Matlis dual to transport the annihilation to the first direct image, and finishes with the chapter's torsion bound. H3: a duality argument with several identifications, written out in full.
